extracted.intended_audience: K–12 mathematics teachers and mathematics educators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for integrating the history of mathematics into classroom teaching to support cognitive, affective, and humanistic learning goals and to make mathematics more engaging and meaningful for students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for integrating history (cognitive, affective, humanistic)
rubrics_metrics.description: The author provided five main reasons for integrating the history of mathematics into teaching, including cognitive, affective, and humanistic aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the history of mathematics for multiple, complementary purposes rather than as an add-on; consider cognitive (understanding), affective (student attitudes), and humanistic (contextualizing mathematics as human activity) reasons when deciding how to incorporate history into lessons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanistic benefit: humanization of mathematical knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: The main utility of the history of mathematics lies in the humanization of mathematical knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present mathematical development as a human endeavor to cultivate appreciation for mathematics and to provide cultural/epistemological context; the author views this humanistic aspect as the most critical reason for using history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cognitive benefit: trigger students' mathematical thinking
rubrics_metrics.description: History can trigger students' mathematical thinking by showing how concepts developed and problems were solved historically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use historical problems, original methods, or the development of ideas to prompt students to reason, conjecture, and understand mathematical concepts more deeply rather than only presenting final proofs or formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affective benefit: cultivate positive attitudes and appreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: History of mathematics can cultivate an attitude of appreciating mathematics among students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage stories, historical motivations, and human elements to improve student engagement and affect toward mathematics, making the subject feel more accessible and meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use history as a platform to develop students' epistemological beliefs
rubrics_metrics.description: History can serve as a platform for developing college students' epistemological beliefs about mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design courses or modules where historical viewpoints and episodes are explicitly used to shape students' beliefs about what mathematics is and how mathematical knowledge is constructed (see referenced studies by the author on epistemological interpretations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate examples from other times and places to broaden curricular perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ geometric and other mathematical approaches from different historical periods and cultures to teach content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include material such as 'geometric approaches to quadratic equations from other times and places' to broaden students' understanding of mathematical diversity and historical development, helping to connect curriculum topics to varied historical contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use primary sources and mathematicians' correspondence to show how mathematics is actually done
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting correspondence or primary historical texts (e.g., Pascal–Fermat correspondence) can reveal how mathematicians reason, argue, and develop ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring original sources, letters, and historically situated arguments into the classroom to demystify mathematical practice and illustrate the process of mathematical discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design interdisciplinary classroom activities combining history with other subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine astronomy, history, and mathematics (and other disciplines) in classroom activities to create richer learning experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create activities that link mathematics with historical scientific problems or cultural artifacts (e.g., navigation, astronomy, art) to provide context and motivate mathematical problems and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply structured strategies for using history (Who? How? What?)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use explicit strategies such as 'Who? How? What? A Strategy for Using History to Teach Mathematics' to frame historical lessons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt lesson-planning frameworks that ask who was involved, how methods were developed, and what was done to teach history-informed mathematics lessons systematically rather than ad hoc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use history to seek relevance and make mathematics more engaging
rubrics_metrics.description: History can be used to seek relevance for students by connecting mathematics to meaningful historical narratives and applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When choosing historical material, prioritize topics and stories that make course content feel relevant to students' interests and show the evolution and applicability of mathematical ideas.
